pool.title: Diagnostic ablation: does the model use neighbour content, or only its position code?
pool.what: Grid over three variants on Fencing, PoznanStreet, Welder, Blocks: (a) gate neighbour memories by object_score_logits / eff_iou instead of taking them unconditionally, (b) vary which temporal-position row the neighbour token borrows (current alias of t-1..t-4, the cond row, rows 3..5, mean), (c) append the neighbour obj_ptr as extra pointer tokens.

A5: neighbour memories bypass the eff_iou frame filter own-view memories pass through. A6: the neighbour obj_ptr, the most natural cross-view presence signal, is never read. Without this grid the paper cannot say what the mechanism exploits, and the observed pattern (neutral-to-slightly-negative on well-tracked cameras, positive only when the own track dies) is equally consistent with 'position only'.

pool.expected_gain: unquantified; the audit's reviewers agreed the neighbour-pointer variant is most promising and that a tpos-row change is out-of-distribution for the frozen encoder

pool.title: Fix TRIM_CACHED_OUTPUTS: the env parse, the dead guard, and the docstring's false safety claim

(1) The parse at demoSCSam3MVOpt/SCSam3VideoInferenceNewMem.py:38 is `os.environ.get(...).strip() not in ("", "0")`, so `"false"`, `"off"`, `"no"` and `"00"` all enable trimming. The audit's own recommendation is "do not enable in interactive demos", but nothing in the code enforces that, and the docstring actively tells a reader a guard protects them when it does not. The published numbers are safe — mvopt-audit.md:100-106 proves trim ON vs OFF is byte-identical across 12 datasets / 12,692 PNGs and on Blocks / 882 PNGs — so this is purely about the interactive path and future callers.

pool.title: Bound-guard (behind a flag) the negative cross-view index that silently wraps

For low `spatial_idx` the sum is negative and Python wraps it to the end of the list, so the first views attend to the last views. Add an explicit `if prev_spatial_idx < 0: continue` — but ONLY behind a default-off flag, and measure both arms.

SCHEDULE P2 (parameterise the cross-view window, enabling an in-package W=0 control) and P4 (the window is one-sided, `range(-4, 0)`) are the same code region, so do them together. Left alone, the next person to read this line will read it as an obvious off-by-one and correct it.

plans.thesis: The blunt read: this project currently has an engineering result and a publishable-looking number, but no defensible claim. Three holes a reviewer finds in an afternoon. (1) The headline is a tie, not a win — 0.8451 vs 0.8434 is +0.0017 against a per-dataset SE of ~0.006 (REPORT E3); the in-session paired bootstrap is 8/15 wins, CI [-0.0080, +0.0109]; under DAVIS-style per-sequence aggregation it is 0.8381 vs 0.8358 and SAM2-vs-OneStage becomes an exact tie; under area-weighted J the effect vanishes entirely (0.9253 vs 0.9254, REPORT E1). (2) The paper's central mechanism has never been ablated — REPORT E2 shows OneStage vs OneStageNew differs in package, sys.path, request shape and session count, and that even the 8 index-0 cameras that receive zero neighbours differ from OneStage on every frame because of the C2 clobber, so there is no "cross-view off" condition anywhere in the existing data. The `range(-4,0)` control has literally never been run. (3) The baseline is not apples-to-apples and not reproducible — SAM 2 runs fill_hole_area=8 and non_overlap off against SAM 3's 0/on at 288 vs 256 low-res (E6), the entire claimed advantage is F (+0.006), the same magnitude as those knobs; and the cited column SegMaskNew1 is the best of six columns whose configs are unrecorded, with the one recheck reproducing SegMaskNew3 instead. Therefore the next stretch of work is NOT for another 0.001 of J&F — chasing it is unwinnable at this effect size. It is for converting an observed difference into an attributed mechanism: measure the effect honestly with paired statistics on the endpoints where it should live (non-reference cameras, neighbour-count bins), build the same-package W=0 control that makes the number attributable, then demonstrate dose-response across W and across neighbour availability. A monotone W curve plus a predicted-and-confirmed recovery in the nb=0 bin (via the two-sided window, which today reaches none of the 8 index-0 cameras, 6 of them references) is a far stronger paper than +0.002 on a headline. One consequence must be accepted up front: the C1/C2 hygiene fixes deliberately change outputs, so the frozen 0.8451 cannot survive as the paper's number. Retire it in Phase 3 and report the hygiene-fixed family end to end.

phases.name: Phase 2 — Can the claim survive arithmetic? (zero GPU)
phases.goal: Rebuild report_jf.py into an instrument that produces every table the paper needs, with confidence intervals, on the endpoints where the mechanism should act — then decide, in writing, whether any endpoint carries the claim.
phases.rationale: This phase costs no GPU and reads entirely from Data/MVSeg/jf_*.json and PNGs already on disk, yet it is the phase that determines whether the paper is viable. Every item is a hole a reviewer finds for free: report_jf.py today has only --raw/--methods/--datasets/--common/--no-missing (verified), so there is no committed script that reproduces the non-reference number (0.8052/0.8093/0.8144), the nb-bin curve (nb=0 -0.0001 → nb=4 +0.0047), the area-weighted J that erases the effect, or any paired statistic. agg-protocol matters because experiments.md:7-27 never states how per-object scores become a headline, and the choice moves the number ~0.007. coverage-matched separates 'segments worse' from 'registers fewer objects' (Blocks 882 vs 1386 PNGs, MATF 1323 vs 2772). onestagenew-column removes a factual misstatement — 9 of the 15 OneStageNew entries are MVOpt output scored under another name. sam2-xview-pair is the cheapest strong evidence available: an independent on/off pair in the SAM 2 lineage giving +0.0014, 11/15 wins, and it costs a code diff plus arithmetic already done. seed-quality-diag is the go/no-go for Phase 6 and is free. cpu-only-tests is scheduled here, not later, because Phase 3 deliberately changes output and needs a diff -rq harness plus a J&F floor in waitAndRunMVSeg.sh (whose only gate today is `grep -q "all runs finished"`, which an all-black mask passes) to tell intended change from accidental breakage across a 20-sweep campaign.
phases.exit_criteria: A single committed report_jf.py regenerates every table in the paper from stored jf_*.json, supporting --split ref|nonref, --bin-by-nb, --area-weighted, --paired (per-camera sign test + bootstrap CI), --ceiling, coverage-matched aggregation, J_inner, and both aggregations (object-pooled and DAVIS per-sequence); runMVSegAll.sh:104 and :111 pass --common; a per-dataset degenerate-seed table exists for all 15 datasets; per-frame J/F curves are dumped and plotted by neighbour count; a written GO/NO-GO memo names which endpoint (if any) shows the cross-view effect outside its CI, and states which single SAM 3 column the paper will report.

phases.name: Phase 3 — Build the control the paper does not have
phases.goal: Produce the first valid in-package cross-view ablation: W=0 vs W=4 on 15 datasets, with the two hygiene defects that contaminate any such comparison removed first.
phases.rationale: This is the load-bearing phase. REPORT.md:237 states outright that no accuracy proposal can be judged before this pair of runs exists. The hygiene fixes must precede the parameterization because the C2 clobber lives inside the neighbour loop, so a naive W=0 switches off the window and the clobber together and isolates nothing (E2). Both fixes are one line each and both are still absent — verified at :1264 (`for s_pos in range(-4, 0)` with no bounds check) and :1273 (still rebinding selected_cond_outputs). closure-track-mode is scheduled here rather than as a nicety because the campaign ahead is roughly 20 sweeps and closure cuts Welder from 553 s to ~60 s and AlexaMeade from 945 to 84 view-frames; it is provably output-identical to `all` once the C1 guard lands (one-sided window, ascending lockstep), and the identity is cheap to verify. The phase must also force the decision the schedule cannot defer: hygiene-fixed W=4 will not equal 0.8451, so the paper picks the hygiene family and retires the frozen number rather than printing a hygiene-fixed W curve beside a frozen headline.
phases.exit_criteria: `diff -rq` shows zero differences between closure and all on Blocks, Fencing and Welder; SegMaskSam3XW0 and SegMaskSam3XW4 exist for all 15 datasets and are scored; the net cross-view effect (XW4 − XW0) is reported with paired CI, non-reference split and nb bins from the Phase 2 instrument; a one-paragraph decision record states that the hygiene-fixed family is the paper's system and that 0.8451 is superseded, with the delta from the frozen run quantified per camera.

phases.name: Phase 4 — Dose-response: turn a tie into a mechanism
phases.goal: Show that the cross-view effect scales with the amount of cross-view information available — across window size, across neighbour count, and across view ordering — and that it costs nothing per view-frame.
phases.rationale: Given an effect that is ~+0.003 with a CI straddling zero, absolute magnitude cannot carry the paper; structure can. A monotone W curve (W ∈ {1,2,6}, hard-capped at 6 by maskmem_tpos_enc's 7 rows) plus the nb-bin curve is a dose-response argument that survives a small effect size. two-sided-window is the strongest single test available because the theory makes a falsifiable prediction: 8 of 36 scored cameras are index 0 and receive zero neighbours, 6 of them are reference cameras, and Fencing's entire -0.021 deficit sits on v0 while the same two objects recover at v9 where four neighbours exist. If the t-1-fallback two-sided window moves the nb=0 bin and nothing else, the mechanism is demonstrated. REPORT P4 labels the Fencing v0 0.80 → 0.86 figure an inference, not a measurement — this phase is what converts it. view-order is here because A1 shows the neighbour set is 'the W predecessors in session-list order' taken from a demo literal, so a multi-view reviewer will ask whether the gain survives a different permutation; a negative result is publishable as a stated limitation, an unasked question is not. timing-matched is nearly free once closure exists and yields a positive result the paper currently cannot state: 0.44 vs 0.56 s per view-frame, cross-view pass 16 vs 15 s — the mechanism is cost-neutral. Ring wrap stays off for the LLFF scenes (Blocks/Fencing/Carpark are open arcs).
phases.exit_criteria: W ∈ {0,1,2,4,6} scored on the 6-dataset sensitivity set with the full 15 for W ∈ {0,4}, reported as a curve with CIs; two-sided W=2 and W=4 runs scored, with the nb=0 bin delta reported separately and Fencing v0 J1-20 stated as measured (target ≥0.85, but the measured value is the deliverable either way); at least two alternative view orderings run on Fencing and PoznanStreet plus a null-effect control; a per-view-frame timing table with matched session counts for OneStage and the cross-view variant.

phases.name: Phase 5 — Make the baseline comparison fair and the identity claim complete
phases.goal: Remove every reviewer objection to the comparison arm: matched post-processing, a named and reproducible baseline configuration, and equivalence evidence on the three datasets where it is currently structurally absent.
phases.rationale: The claimed SAM 3 advantage is almost entirely boundary F (0.8727 → 0.8820 on the 12-dataset subset, BRIEF:47-57), and E6 establishes that three post-processing settings differing between the arms are the same magnitude as that gap. Until they are matched, the paper's one clear win is unattributed. sam2-provenance is the companion problem: the baseline claim selects the best of six SAM 2 columns whose generating scripts and configs are nowhere recorded, and the 2026-09-04 recheck reproduces SegMaskNew3 (0.8060/0.8644/0.8352) rather than the cited SegMaskNew1 (0.8084/0.8675/0.8380) — an unanswerable question if asked. fill-hole-area is the symmetric half: matching can be done from either side, and running SAM 3 at 8 and 16 costs two sweeps and tells you which direction the knob points. heavy3-equivalence closes the last claim the paper will make that has no control: the byte-identity proof for the memory optimizations covers 12 datasets / 12,692 PNGs but cannot cover AlexaMeadeExhibit, CoffeeMartini and FlameSteak because the unoptimized code cannot run them — precisely the three datasets that make '15/15 complete' a selling point. Restrict frames, never cameras (`--track-cams written` changes the model for NewMem-family algorithms and raises IndexError at output_dicts[-4]).
phases.exit_criteria: SegMaskNew1_matched exists for 15 datasets with apply_postprocessing=False and non_overlap_masks=True, scored, with the SAM2-vs-SAM3 F difference recomputed and the residual attributed or reassigned; a provenance table names the script, imports and config for each of the six SAM 2 columns and one column is re-run from source and reproduced; SAM 3 fill_hole ∈ {0,8,16} measured on the 6-dataset set; a frame-restricted identity run on the three heavy datasets reports either zero PNG differences against baseline-onestagenew or the divergence found.

phases.name: Phase 6 — Recover the largest measured loss and report the ceiling
phases.goal: Fix the one failure mode with a quantified upside, and give the benchmark an upper reference so the remaining error can be split between cross-view seeding and tracking.
phases.rationale: seed-repair is the only accuracy item in the whole backlog with a number derived from measurement rather than inference: Welder's entire -0.034 deficit versus SAM 2 is camera_0004, where the spatial pass seeds objects 8 and 14 at 4 px and 7 px against GT of 13,268 and 18,899 px while SAM 2 seeds the same three at IoU 0.94/0.93/0.90 — worth Welder +0.035~0.04, roughly +0.0025 on the 15-dataset headline. It is scheduled after the mechanism work, not before, because A3 also establishes that cross-view memory demonstrably cannot overturn a bad seed (ΔJ +0.0004), so this is a stage-1 repair that improves the number without touching the paper's mechanism story — valuable, but not what the claim rests on. Phase 2's free diagnostic gates it: if degenerate seeds are rare outside Welder, scope shrinks to a single dataset result. crossview-seed-oracle turns E4's confound into a reported ceiling — the reference camera is already implicitly a GT-seeded VOS run (J0 0.962), so extending that to all three scored cameras answers 'how much of the remaining error is seeding' directly and bounds seed-repair's headroom. ceiling-refrule is a protocol correction, not evidence for the method — 1,579 of 21,651 scored (obj,frame) pairs (7.3%) are unreachable by any method under the max-id reference rule — so it is reported as a ceiling column and a rank-invariant ablation, never as a gain. Keep SPATIAL_START_IMPLICIT=1 throughout: an explicit start index collapsed Blocks 0.7484 → 0.2827 once already.
phases.exit_criteria: RepairSeeds runs on Welder, Blocks, MATF, PoznanStreet and Painter with Carpark and Frog as controls; Welder camera_0004 objects 8/14 reach J ≥ 0.8 or the failure is characterised, and controls move within ±0.001; a per-camera GT-seeded oracle row exists for 15 datasets and is reported as the ceiling in every table; the count-rule reference ablation reproduces the structural-zero drops (Blocks 203→63, MATF 372→231, PoznanStreet 42→0) across all three methods with the ranking unchanged.

phases.name: Phase 7 — Robustness, error bars, and the external-reference decision
phases.goal: Produce the paper's honest variance estimate and settle whether it can be positioned against anything outside this repository.
phases.rationale: Runs are bit-identical run-to-run (REPORT:40-44), so there is no seed variance to report and reference choice is the only variance source available — yet the headline rests on exactly one reference draw per dataset, and that draw determines both a third of the score (the reference camera is nearly GT-seeded) and which objects are reachable at all. If the spread across reference choices exceeds the effect, that must appear in the paper rather than in a reviewer's report. external-baseline is the hole with the highest probability of being fatal at a good venue: every number in experiments.md is the authors' code against the authors' earlier code, and the only directory resembling a competitor (ConMask) is GT re-encoded per object, not a method. Scope the cheap half first — teaching eval_jf.py the flat-GT layout makes the existing SA3D/SAM2 folders on 9 variant scenes scoreable in hours — then take an explicit written decision on whether an off-the-shelf VOS run (SAM 2.1 / XMem / Cutie under per-camera GT seeds, framed as an upper reference rather than a like-for-like competitor) is in scope for the target venue. neighbor-objptr is the single token-conditioning variant all three reviewers converged on and the only one not expected to be null or out-of-distribution; it runs on the P12 4-dataset grid against Phase 3's clean W=4 reference and is included here as the one remaining upside shot, with a pre-registered success bar.
phases.exit_criteria: Reference camera forced to each of the three scored cameras on at least six datasets for both SAM 3 and SAM 2, reported as mean ± spread beside the effect size; the 9 variant scenes scored against existing SA3D/SAM2 folders and tabulated; a written venue-scoped decision on the external VOS baseline with an owner and, if in scope, a protocol statement; neighbor-objptr measured on Fencing/PoznanStreet/Welder/Blocks against the pre-registered bar (>+0.005 on non-reference cameras with no reference-camera loss) and accepted or rejected on that bar.

plans.thesis: The method's advantage is currently unmeasurable, not small: MVOpt 0.8451 vs SAM 2's best 0.8434 is +0.0017 against a between-dataset SE of ~0.006 (REPORT E3), and the +0.0032 cross-view effect on the 12-dataset subset is carried by 3-4 small objects in 3 of 36 cameras — freezing those three objects to OneStage values returns 0.8497 to 0.8468, and area-weighted J is 0.9253 vs 0.9254, i.e. the effect vanishes entirely under area weighting (REPORT E1). So the next stretch of work is not "add mechanism". It is, in order: (1) build an endpoint that can resolve a 0.005 effect and run the zero-GPU diagnostic that decides the biggest accuracy item — three days, no GPU; (2) recover the two measured losses to SAM 2, Welder −0.034 and Fencing −0.021, because these are the only places where a competing system demonstrably does better on the same data, which means the ceiling is proven rather than hypothesised; (3) only then produce the in-package W=0 vs W=4 control, without which nothing about cross-view memory is attributable (REPORT E2: even the 8 index-0 cameras that receive zero neighbours differ from OneStage every frame, because of the C2 pointer clobber, so no camera in the current data is a "cross-view off" condition). Losses first, mechanism second, protocol third. Two facts shape every phase boundary: the C1/C2 hygiene fixes deliberately change published output, so W=4-with-hygiene is a different system from the frozen 0.8451 and the paper must pick one family and report it end to end; and GPU is not the constraint — a 15-dataset sweep is 35-90 min on one card, so human time and the number of *interpretable* comparisons, not compute, set the pace.

phases.name: Instrument first — an endpoint that can resolve 0.005
phases.goal: Make the benchmark able to tell a real gain from noise, run the zero-GPU diagnostic that decides the single highest-evidence accuracy item, and make the sweep infrastructure safe for the ~15-20 runs that follow.
phases.rationale: Nothing downstream is judgeable without this. REPORT E1 shows the reported gain is 3-4 objects and disappears under area weighting; E3 puts the per-dataset SE at ~0.006 and notes runMVSegAll.sh:104,:111 still call report_jf.py without --common, so the AVERAGE row mixes 12- and 15-dataset denominators; E4 shows a third of every score is the reference camera, which is GT-seeded single-view VOS (J at frame 0 = 0.962) and lifts every method ~0.04 while diluting the multi-view signal — non-reference-only is 0.8052/0.8093/0.8144, where the delta over SAM 2 is roughly +0.009, five times the headline. agg-protocol is here because the aggregation is unstated and load-bearing: report_jf.py:56-92 pools every (camera,object) J within a dataset, and DAVIS-style per-sequence aggregation gives 0.8358/0.8357/0.8381 versus the dataset-mean 0.8434/0.8427/0.8451 — a ~0.007 swing that makes SAM2-vs-OneStage an exact tie. seed-quality-diag is the go/no-go for Phase 1 and REPORT P5's own verification plan says to run it first: it counts degenerate seeds per dataset from PNGs already on disk, bounding the seed-repair upside beyond the one camera A3 measured. memcap-two-scripts is two lines and is the only item whose failure mode takes the machine down rather than the run — operations.md:27 records two reboots, and runMVSegAll.sh:62 is still `docker run --rm --gpus all --shm-size=32g` with no cap (verified). onestagenew-column closes the mask-manufacturing trap before I start sweeping: the three heavy datasets have no SegMaskSam3OneStageNew directory, so runMVSeg.py:298-300's already-exists guard cannot fire and an --algo OneStageNew sweep would silently retro-validate the file. retire-log-truthful and push-and-purge-token-image are minutes each: the first removes a false signal from the log anyone reads during an OOM triage, the second pushes b427b45 and deletes scsam3:pre-secret-backup, which still carries the HF token in three cleartext layers.

phases.name: Recover the Welder loss — the only quantified accuracy win
phases.goal: Turn the measured Welder −0.034 deficit against SAM 2 into roughly zero by detecting and repairing degenerate cross-view seeds, attributed against the still-frozen 0.8451 baseline.
phases.rationale: This is the highest expected accuracy per unit of effort on the whole list, and the only accuracy item with a proven ceiling rather than an inferred one. A3 is measured, not reasoned: the spatial pass seeds Welder camera_0004 objects 8 and 14 with 4 px and 7 px against GT of 13,268 and 18,899 px, and object 12 at IoU 0.184, while the SAM 2 spatial pass seeds the same three at IoU 0.94/0.93/0.90 and tracks them at J 0.93/0.93/0.90. So a competing system already achieves the target on this exact data — the failure is in stage 1, not in the tracker. A3 also establishes why nothing else can fix it: the seed is pinned into cond memory and the cond object pointer, and cross-view memory moves it by ΔJ +0.0004 even though views 0/1/2 hold the object, so temporal cross-view memory is structurally unable to repair this class of failure. P5 quantifies the payoff at Welder +0.035~0.04, ≈+0.0025 on the 15-dataset headline, which alone would roughly triple the current margin over SAM 2. It runs first, before the hygiene fixes, for two reasons: it touches runMVSeg's spatial pass and not the temporal gather, so its effect is cleanly attributable against a published number; and it is robust to the Phase-2 ablation outcome — if W=4 vs W=0 comes back null, which E1's statistics make plausible, Welder is still banked. spatial-start-docstring rides along because RepairSeeds re-propagates the spatial session, which is exactly the path where an explicit start index collapsed Blocks from 0.7484 to 0.2827 (investigations-closed #4), and runMVSeg.py:201-205's docstring currently describes the opposite of what the code does.
phases.exit_criteria: Precondition logged before any code: the refine branch at SCSam3VideoInference.py:1855-1870 confirmed to add a cond frame to the SAME tracker state (use_stateless_refinement=False) rather than creating a new one — this is the reviewer split REPORT P5 flags. Then: Welder camera_0004 objects 8 and 14 reach J ≥0.8 and object 12 ≥0.6; Welder dataset J&F ≥0.875; control datasets Carpark and Frog move by ≤±0.001; a 15-dataset re-score is reported with the Phase-0 paired CI and nonref split. Every repair run uses implicit start (SPATIAL_START_IMPLICIT=1) and --memory=90g. If the bar is missed, the item closes with the measured post-repair camera_0004 J as the number that killed it, and the area test's known blind spot (object 12: 2,633 px but IoU 0.18, so displaced rather than small) is reported as the reason.

phases.name: Hygiene, then the control the entire claim rests on
phases.goal: Remove the two confirmed defects in the cross-view gather, cut sweep cost ~5x, and produce the first in-package W=0 vs W=4 pair — the comparison without which no cross-view claim is attributable.
phases.rationale: C2 is unambiguously wrong and cheap to fix: SCSam3TrackerPredictorNewMem.py:1273 (verified still `selected_cond_outputs, unselected_cond_outputs1 = ...`) rebinds a view's own cond outputs to a neighbour's, and that value is consumed as the cond object pointer at :1335-1341, so views 0..3 use the LAST camera's seed pointer — and where that object was zero-mask seeded the pointer is no_obj_ptr with object_score_logits = −10, an explicit 'object absent' signal injected into a view where the object is present. C1 (line 1264, `for s_pos in range(-4, 0)`, verified with no bounds check) is what makes that dead fallback execute every frame, so the two ship together per SCHEDULE:423. Expected headline movement is small and bounded — E2 measures index-0 camera means differing by at most ±0.0015 today and that difference IS the C2 effect, so ≲0.0004 on the headline — but per-(obj,frame) |ΔJ| reaches 0.49 (Fencing v0 f17), and the fix is a precondition for every interpretable window measurement. closure-track-mode is the throughput multiplier that pays for phases 3-6: it is provably output-identical to `all` once C1 lands (the window is one-sided and lockstep ascends, so scored view v depends only on views 0..v), and takes Welder 553 s → ~60 s and AlexaMeadeExhibit 945 → 84 view-frames. cpu-only-tests belongs here rather than anywhere else because its N=3 wrap/clobber cases are precisely the edits being made, and its J&F floor gate closes waitAndRunMVSeg.sh:55-59, whose only current check is `grep -q "all runs finished"` — a gate an all-black mask passes, which matters now that ~15 unattended sweeps are ahead. xw0-control is REPORT row 3+4 and REPORT.md:235 states plainly that no accuracy proposal can be judged before it exists.
phases.exit_criteria: `diff -rq` between --track-cams closure and --track-cams all is empty on Blocks, Fencing and Welder; pytest green including the N=3 IndexError/wrap/clobber cases, parse_action_history at ref = N−1, processing_order over 21 frames, and an AST undefined-name pass; SegMaskSam3XW0 and SegMaskSam3XW4 both complete 15/15 under --memory=90g --memory-swap=90g and --track-cams closure; the noise-floor check passes — all 36 cameras show |ΔJ| < 0.001 between XW0 and the matched-session OneStage row; and the XW4 − XW0 delta is reported on the Phase-0 endpoints (nonref, nb-bin, paired CI), not on the headline alone. A written decision is recorded at phase end: hygiene-fixed W=4 is a different system from the frozen 0.8451, so the paper adopts one family and reports it end to end — never a hygiene-fixed W-curve printed beside the frozen headline.

phases.name: Take the mechanism to the cameras that structurally never receive it
phases.goal: Test whether the cross-view recovery observed at Fencing v9 transfers to index-0 cameras via a boundary-clipped two-sided window with a t−1 fallback, then map W sensitivity.
phases.rationale: This is the largest structural headroom in the method, and the evidence is half measured and half inferred — the split matters. Measured (A2): Fencing's entire deficit sits on v0, J1-20 0.794 vs SAM 2 0.890, objects 3 and 4 at J 0.32/0.23; the identical two objects recover to 0.55/0.58 at v9, where four neighbours exist. Measured (A1): the nb-bin ΔJ is +0.0047 at nb=4 (21 cameras) and −0.0001 at nb=0 (8 cameras), so the effect tracks neighbour availability. Measured: 8 of 36 scored cameras are index 0 and 6 of those are reference cameras, so a third of the benchmark score never receives the mechanism at all. Inferred, and REPORT.md:165 labels it so explicitly: that giving v0 neighbours produces the v9 recovery, i.e. v0 J 0.80 → ~0.86. THE CHEAP EXPERIMENT THAT DECIDES IT, before building any plumbing: run Fencing alone with the t−1 fallback enabled and W=1 — one dataset, minutes of GPU. If v0 objects 3 and 4 do not move at all, the transfer hypothesis is dead and only the W curve is worth finishing; if they move, the full two-sided refactor is justified. Note a hard structural constraint: a true same-frame two-sided window is impossible under lockstep, so only the t−1-fallback form is implementable, and the higher view's t−1 always exists from the second frame onward. Two-sided W=4 costs +115% memory tokens, transient only (M1: the cross-view prompt is tens of MB inside a 38-44 GiB budget). xview-window-param needs no new code after xw0-control — it is sweeps only, W ∈ {1,2,6} on the six effect datasets per REPORT row 5, capped at W ≤ 6 because maskmem_tpos_enc has exactly 7 rows. The refactor also fixes C8's stale seq_len (computed at :1283 from own-view feats, reused at :1315 for the neighbour branch).
phases.exit_criteria: The single-dataset Fencing decider is run and reported BEFORE the refactor, with the per-frame IoU of v0 objects 3 and 4 as the readout. If it passes, the full two-sided run must clear Fencing v0 J1-20 ≥0.85, show nb=0-bin ΔJ ≠ 0, and lose ≤0.005 on cameras with index ≥4; ring wrap stays off for Blocks, Fencing and Carpark (open-arc LLFF poses_bounds) and is enabled per-dataset only where the layout is verified. Defaults ship one-sided/no-ring so the Phase-2 numbers still reproduce. The W curve is published for W ∈ {0,1,2,4,6} on the six effect datasets with monotonicity stated either way — a flat curve is a reportable result, not a failure.

phases.name: Protocol ceiling and the two cheap untested knobs
phases.goal: Raise the achievable ceiling for every method by fixing the reference rule, and spend two cheap shots on the untested knobs that could still move boundary F and open the unused cross-view channel.
phases.rationale: ceiling-refrule is evidence-backed from ground truth alone and is the largest single number-mover left, but with an honesty condition attached. A7: runMVSeg.py:111 is still `n = int(np.max(img))` (verified) while the docstring claims 'most objects'; an object absent from the reference seed frame gets a zero prompt, is dropped by the zero-area filter at SCSam3VideoInference.py:464, never registers, and scores J=F=0 on every frame. From GT: 1,579 of 21,651 scored (obj,frame) pairs — 7.3% — are unreachable by ANY method, and the count rule takes Blocks 203→63, MATF 372→231, PoznanStreet 42→0, Painter 99→61, FacePaint 105→63, lifting the achievable-J ceiling by +0.128 on Blocks, +0.087 on MATF, +0.061 on FacePaint. The condition: P8 states this lifts every method equally and leaves the ranking unchanged, so it raises J&F without raising the margin — it must be reported as a protocol change with the ceiling column, and the SAM 2 baselines re-run under the same rule. Two of three reviewers also rejected the related 'tie-break toward a centre view' motivation, so adopt the count rule only. fill-hole-area is the cheapest untested knob in the entire pipeline and is itself the experiment: SCSam3Video.py:17,:20 monkey-patch it to 0 over a builder default of 16 while SAM 2 runs with 8, and hole filling is precisely a boundary-F knob in the component where SAM 3 already leads (F 0.8727 → 0.8820). The docs assert no direction — treat the sign as unknown, run fill ∈ {8,16}, two sweeps. neighbor-objptr is the one token-conditioning variant all three reviewers converged on (A6): in SAM 3 the object pointer carries the object/no-object decision, it is the most natural cross-view presence channel, the 256-d tensors are already GPU-resident, and :1335-1368 reads only output_dicts[spatial_idx] — the channel is simply empty. It needs the Phase-2 XW4 to read against.
phases.exit_criteria: Each of the three reports against a bar declared before its run. ceiling-refrule: --reference {count,maxid,<cam>} added at runMVSeg.py:111 and runMVSegForSam2.py:78-79 with maxid as default so current numbers reproduce; seed_coverage.json emitted; report_jf.py --ceiling column in every table; the predicted structural-zero counts reproduced; all three methods re-run on the five affected datasets and all three rise together with the ranking unchanged; SPATIAL_START_IMPLICIT=1 on every run. fill-hole-area: adopted only if the 15-dataset Δ exceeds +0.002 AND has the same sign on the nonref split; the value surfaced in the runMVSeg banner either way. neighbor-objptr: adopted only if it clears >+0.005 on non-reference cameras with no reference-camera loss on the 4-dataset grid (Fencing, PoznanStreet, Welder, Blocks); otherwise closed with its measured number.

phases.name: Make the SAM 2 comparison apples-to-apples
phases.goal: Settle whether the SAM 3 advantage survives a matched baseline, pin down which SAM 2 system the paper is actually citing, and add a second independent estimate of the mechanism.
phases.rationale: This is the biggest single threat to the headline, and it is cheap to retire. The SAM 3 edge is almost entirely boundary F (12-dataset 0.8727 → 0.8820, i.e. +0.006) and E6 establishes that three post-processing settings differ by the same magnitude: SAM 2 uses fill_hole_area=8 applied at low-res 256² (~250 px full-res) while SAM 3 forces 0; SAM 3 applies the non-overlap constraint to its output and SAM 2 does not; low-res is 288 vs 256, which cannot be matched and must be stated. A matched SAM 2 could close the F gap entirely — better to know that before the claim is written than after. sam2-provenance because the baseline claim selects the best of six columns whose configs are nowhere recorded, and those columns are not near-duplicates (Dog 0.7662 vs 0.9089; FlameSteak 0.4627 vs 0.7835); worse, the 2026-09-04 recheck reproduces SegMaskNew3 (0.8060/0.8644/0.8352 on CoffeeMartini) and NOT the cited headline column SegMaskNew1 (0.8084/0.8675/0.8380). Picking the strongest baseline is the conservative choice, but the paper cannot currently say which system produced it. sam2-xview-pair is hours and zero GPU for a genuinely valuable result: the SAM 2 lineage has its own cross-view on/off pair (SegMask1 from SCSam2Video, SegMaskNew3 from SCSam2VideoNew), and if the diff shows they differ ONLY in the cross-view memory then the paired delta is already computable — +0.0014, 11/15 wins — an independent replication of the same mechanism at the same size in a second model family. timing-matched turns a session-count artefact into a positive result: E5 shows '2-3x slower' is 46 sessions vs 3, and per view-frame OneStageNew is actually faster (0.44 s vs 0.56 s) with the cross-view pass at 15 s vs 16 s — cross-view memory is not measurably more expensive, which the paper currently cannot state. closure-track-mode from Phase 2 makes the matched-session run cheap.
phases.exit_criteria: SegMaskNew1_matched exists for 15 datasets with apply_postprocessing=False and non_overlap_masks=True, re-scored, and the SAM2-vs-SAM3 F difference recomputed and reported both matched and unmatched, with the 288-vs-256 low-res mismatch stated as unmatchable; the generating script and config of every cited SAM 2 folder is documented and at least the cited column is re-run and reproduced, or the citation is moved to the column that reproduces; the SAM 2 on/off pair is either published as an independent replication or explicitly disqualified with the structural difference that disqualifies it (SAM 2 batches all objects into one state per camera, SCSam2VideoNew.py:123-142, versus SAM 3's per-object states); per-view-frame timing and peak GPU/host RAM reported with matched session counts, cross-view pass separated.

phases.name: Error bars, ceilings, and the one hole in the equivalence proof
phases.goal: Quantify the two variance components the headline currently hides, add the upper reference the benchmark has never had, and close the place where the byte-identity proof structurally cannot reach.
phases.rationale: Runs are bit-identical run-to-run — 41 of 45 cameras across two sweeps (REPORT.md:40-44) — so there is no seed variance to report, and reference choice and view ordering are the only error bars available. Each is plausibly larger than the effect being claimed. ref-view-sensitivity: the reference camera is one of the three scored cameras, is nearly GT-seeded (J0 0.962), and determines which objects are reachable at all (7.3% unreachable under the current rule), yet there is exactly one draw per dataset. view-order: A1 shows the result encodes the perms literal (sam3_demoVideo.py:17 is [0..7,16..31,8..15], and Dog's perms skip cameras outright) rather than camera geometry, and the measured pattern matches — only high-index cameras gain, Fencing v4 +0.001 vs v9 +0.066, PoznanStreet v4 +0.005 vs v8 +0.029. Any reviewer of a multi-view paper asks whether the gain survives a different ordering; a negative result here is itself publishable as a limitation. crossview-seed-oracle gives the benchmark its missing upper reference and bounds the headroom every seeding proposal chases — it is already implicitly measured for one of the three cameras (E4), so extending it to all three converts a confound into a reported ceiling. frames-horizon is CPU-only and produces the figure that shows the mechanism acting rather than asserted: with num_maskmem=7 over 21 frames the memory bank reaches steady state around frame 7, and Fencing v9 obj 3 holds IoU 0.63 from frame 8 onward, so a rescue mechanism should show a widening gap. heavy3-equivalence closes the one structural gap in the memory-optimization proof: 12 datasets / 12,692 PNGs are verified byte-identical, but the original code cannot run at all on AlexaMeadeExhibit, CoffeeMartini and FlameSteak, so the three hardest of the 15 headline entries have no equivalence control — exactly where it matters most.
phases.exit_criteria: The headline is reported as mean ± spread over three reference choices per dataset (using the --reference flag from Phase 4, SPATIAL_START_IMPLICIT=1 throughout), and that spread is stated next to every claimed effect size; ordering sensitivity reported for at least two alternative view orders on Fencing and PoznanStreet plus a null control (Frog or Carpark); the GT-seeded per-camera oracle appears as a ceiling row in every table; per-frame J curves are plotted per method split by neighbour count, with J_inner reported alongside; and a FRAMES-restricted (never camera-restricted — --track-cams written changes the model and raises IndexError at output_dicts[-4]) identity check against git tag baseline-onestagenew on the three heavy datasets reports either zero differences on the prefix or the divergence found, run under --memory=90g --memory-swap=90g.

plans.thesis: The next stretch of work is not about making the number bigger — it is about making the number defensible and the codebase safe to change. Right now the project has a real result (J&F 0.8451 over 15 datasets) protected by nothing: `Data/` is gitignored so mtime is the sole provenance for every scored mask (experiments.md:141); the seven shipped memory optimizations rest on seven "nobody reads this value" invariants with zero assertions and zero tests guarding them (mvopt-audit.md:110-125, and I confirmed there is not a single test_*.py, conftest.py, pytest.ini or CI workflow anywhere in the repo); the full-sweep entry point `runMVSegAll.sh:62` still runs uncapped on a host that has already been rebooted twice by RAM exhaustion (operations.md:27); one commit carrying the token-free Dockerfile is unpushed; and a `scsam3:pre-secret-backup` image with three cleartext HF_TOKEN layers is still on disk. Meanwhile the headline advantage itself is roughly a quarter of the between-dataset SE (~0.006 per REPORT E3) and vanishes entirely under area weighting (0.9253 vs 0.9254, REPORT E1) — so before spending a month on accuracy work, we should spend a week on the zero-GPU statistics that tell us whether there is an effect to defend at all. The ordering therefore runs: preserve the artifacts (hours) → read the record honestly with no GPU and no code change (one week, and it can kill or redirect everything downstream) → make the code tell the truth and put a test harness under the seven invariants (two weeks) → verify the SAM 2 comparison without touching the method → and only then reach the fork point where C1/C2 hygiene deliberately changes published output. Every accuracy proposal in the audit is downstream of that fork, because REPORT.md:235 is explicit that no accuracy claim can be attributed until the in-package W=0 vs W=4 control exists.

phases.name: Phase 0 — Preserve what exists
phases.goal: Make the current verified state impossible to lose to a reboot, a push failure, or an uncapped sweep, and retire the last live credential on this machine. Nothing here touches inference code, so nothing here can change a number.
phases.rationale: Three independent single-command losses are currently possible. (1) `git status -sb` reads `## main...origin/main [ahead 1]` — b427b45, the commit that removes the HF-token build dependency, exists only locally; a disk failure loses the fix and leaves GitHub advertising the token-dependent Dockerfile. (2) open-items.md:48 names /tmp/sibling_backup as the only copy of the unpatched sibling packages and warns it vanishes on reboot; that is both alarmist and wrong — the originals are in git at 99c05c7 (3232d3e is the patching commit), so `git tag baseline-siblings 99c05c7`, mirroring the existing `baseline-onestagenew` (README.md:15-20), converts a volatile revert path into a permanent one for the cost of one command, and the doc line should be corrected in place. (3) operations.md:19-31 marks runMVSegAll.sh and launch_container.sh with ★ precisely because they lack the `--memory=90g --memory-swap=90g` that runMVOptThree.sh:13 and runForSam2Three.sh:13 carry; I confirmed both are still bare (`docker run --rm --gpus all --shm-size=32g \` and `docker run --shm-size=64g --gpus all -it --rm …`). runMVSegAll.sh is the entry point most likely to be invoked by someone who has not read operations.md, and it is the only trap whose failure mode takes the machine down rather than the run. Setting memory-swap equal to memory zeroes swap so the cgroup OOM killer fires at 90 GiB and leaves a readable log — SCHEDULE:400's truncated FlameSteak line ('11/22 [25:21<1:14:43]', no traceback) is what happens without it. Separately, `scsam3:latest` was rebuilt 2026-09-04T14:13:16 with 0 hf_token hits, so operations.md:151-154 (trap 7) is now stale and should say so — but `docker history scsam3:pre-secret-backup --no-trunc` still yields three layers holding `hf_ShVKFypk…` in cleartext, so the exposure moved rather than closed. Token revocation itself stays with the user (open-items.md:25).

phases.name: Phase 1 — Read the record honestly (zero GPU)
phases.goal: Compute, from files already on disk, what the result actually is — with confidence intervals, on the endpoints the mechanism is supposed to act on — and pin the provenance of every mask that produced it. This phase can redirect or kill everything downstream and cannot break anything, which is why it comes before the expensive work.
phases.rationale: The headline is 0.8451 vs SAM 2's 0.8434 — a gap of 0.0017 against a per-dataset SE of about 0.006 (REPORT E3). Paired statistics computed in-session put MVOpt minus SegMaskNew1 at +0.0016 with 8/15 wins and a 95% bootstrap CI of [-0.0080, +0.0109]; area-weighted J is 0.9253 vs 0.9254, i.e. the entire effect disappears once eval_jf.py:183-188's per-object unweighted average is corrected for area (REPORT E1); and freezing three small objects to OneStage values collapses 0.8497 to 0.8468. A reviewer will derive all of this in one afternoon, so it belongs in the paper as 'comparable, with the gain concentrated where the mechanism is supposed to act' rather than as a headline win. The endpoint that actually carries the claim is the non-reference table — REPORT E4 shows one of the three scored cameras per dataset is the reference, seeded from a GT round-trip (J at frame 0 = 0.962), so a third of the score is GT-seeded single-view VOS diluting the multi-view signal; non-reference-only the numbers are 0.8052 / 0.8093 / 0.8144 and the delta over SAM 2 is roughly +0.009, five times the headline. None of these values is reproducible today: report_jf.py has exactly five flags (--raw/--methods/--datasets/--common/--no-missing) and eval_jf.py:186 already computes J_inner that nothing reports. The aggregation itself is undocumented and load-bearing — report_jf.py:56-92 pools every (camera, object) J within a dataset then takes an unweighted mean over datasets, while the DAVIS-style per-sequence mean over 45 sequences gives 0.8358 / 0.8357 / 0.8381, disagreeing by ~0.007 and turning SAM2-vs-OneStage into an exact tie. Coverage is a second confound: Blocks exports 882 PNGs (SAM 3) vs 1386 (SAM 2), MATF 1323 vs 2772, and eval_jf.py:158-161 scores an absent mask as empty — correct DAVIS protocol, but part of the reported gap is registration coverage, and the existing 'exported only' path evaluates to nan (experiments.md caveat 3). seed-quality-diag is here because SCHEDULE:427 makes it the explicit zero-cost precondition for seed-repair: count degenerate seeds per dataset from the frame-0 PNGs already on disk, so Phase 5's biggest bet is a decision rather than a hope. mask-provenance-manifest anchors all of it — Data/ is in .gitignore:172, `Data/MVSeg/*/SegMaskSam3OneStageNew/` was produced by code that now exists only at tag baseline-onestagenew (README.md:22-24), and runMVSeg.py:298-300's overwrite guard requires the directory to already exist and be non-empty, so an `--algo OneStageNew` sweep would silently manufacture masks for exactly the three heavy datasets the paper reports as unfinishable (experiments.md:89-93). That guard must be hardened before any sweep in Phase 3 or 4 writes anything. onestagenew-column is a pure reporting decision: all 45 OneStageNew and MVOpt entries are identical and 9 of the 15-dataset entries are MVOpt output scored under the OneStageNew name, so 'OneStageNew ran 15 datasets' is a false statement currently in the record. ceiling-refrule's free half — the GT-only achievable ceiling, 1,579 of 21,651 scored (obj, frame) pairs unreachable by any method under the max-id rule — belongs in every table so MATF and Blocks stop reading as tracking failures; the count-rule re-runs are deferred to Phase 5.
phases.exit_criteria: A committed script regenerates every number in a revised experiments.md from Data/MVSeg/jf_*.json with no manual steps, including per-dataset paired deltas, sign tests and bootstrap CIs for both SAM2-vs-SAM3 and OneStage-vs-MVOpt; report_jf.py supports --split, --bin-by-nb, --area-weighted, --paired and surfaces J_inner, and runMVSegAll.sh:104,:111 pass --common; both aggregations (object-pooled and per-sequence) and the coverage-matched aggregation appear side by side; a per-dataset degenerate-seed census exists with counts for all 15 datasets; every frozen mask tree and jf_*.json has a sha256 manifest naming its git revision, runner and trim-flag state, and runMVSeg.py refuses to write into a method folder whose manifest names a different revision; experiments.md reports one SAM 3 column and its three caveats are mechanically checkable rather than remembered.

phases.name: Phase 2 — Make the code tell the truth and guard the seven invariants
phases.goal: Put a CPU-only test harness under every invariant the memory work depends on, and fix the places where the source actively misleads a maintainer, so that Phase 4's deliberate output change happens against a harness rather than against hope. No behaviour on the benchmark path changes in this phase.
phases.rationale: mvopt-audit.md:110-125 states that each of S1-S7 rests on an invariant of the form 'nobody reads this value' and that no assertion or test guards any of them; the gap is wider than the audit says, because I confirmed the repo has no test files, no .github/workflows, no pytest.ini and no conftest.py at all — the only .github content is copilot-instructions.md, and test.py is four lines printing dict lengths. The sharpest invariant is S3: mvopt-audit.md:119 notes torch.where and torch.stack pass meta tensors through silently, so a future 'offload the tracker state to CPU' optimization fails with `Cannot copy out of meta tensor` far from its cause; and mvopt-audit.md:124-125 warns these packages copied upstream files rather than inheriting, so an upstream SAM 3 bump will not surface as a merge conflict — the meta placeholder just quietly meets new code that reads it. SCHEDULE:223 says the same of S4. Left alone, seven changes worth all fifteen datasets completing are protected only by the current call order, and the first reordering fails at hour three of a sweep. The tests are cheap because the interesting logic is pure Python: request-key handling, parse_action_history with ref = N-1, processing_order over 21 frames, the N=3 IndexError, seeding parity, and an AST pass for undefined names that would have caught C6. That AST pass is why dead-api-cleanup lands in this phase rather than later — the four undefined `Sam3VideoPredictorMultiGPU` references (SCSam3VideoPredictorNewMem.py:397,:476; SCSam3VideoPredictor.py:391,:470) would fail it on day one. The truth-telling fixes are the other half. runMVSeg.py:201-205's docstring says the start view 'is spelled out here' while the code six lines below adds the key only `if not SPATIAL_START_IMPLICIT`, which defaults to 1 — and investigations-closed.md #4 records that believing the docstring and flipping the flag drops Blocks from 0.7484 to 0.2827, silently, with masks never generated at all. Six datasets have the last index in cam_list (Blocks 9/10, Carpark 8/9, Fencing 9/10, MATF 9/10, Painter 15/16, PoznanStreet 8/9), so Phase 5's reference-rule change puts four more into range; c3-latent-guard converts that silent collapse into an immediate abort and is covered by the same test suite. runMVSeg.py:339-342 prints 'spatial model retired' whenever the method merely exists, and patch-matrix.md:64-66 shows demoSCSam3OneStage's copy is inert because that folder builds no spatial predictor — so the first log anyone reads during an OOM says 3.2 GiB was released when nothing was built. S7's docstring is the third: it advertises two guards protecting the interactive path, but mvopt-audit.md:67-70 proves the propagation_full guard can never fire because add_prompt always precedes the first propagation, and the env parse at SCSam3VideoInferenceNewMem.py:38 treats 'false', 'off', 'no' and '00' as ON. Batch numbers are safe — trim ON vs OFF is byte-identical across 12 datasets / 12,692 PNGs and on Blocks / 882 PNGs (mvopt-audit.md:100-106) — so this is purely closing a silent, permanent mask-corruption path for interactive and future callers.
phases.exit_criteria: `pytest` runs green from a cold clone with no GPU and no model weights, in under a minute; deliberately reintroducing the C1 wrap, the C2 clobber, a numeric read of the S1 sentinel, or a `.cpu()` on the S3 meta placeholder each fails a named test; the AST undefined-name pass is clean across all five demo packages; waitAndRunMVSeg.sh gates on an eval plus a J&F floor rather than only `grep -q 'all runs finished'` (which an all-black mask passes today); RetireSpatialPredictor returns a real result and the log prints only on an actual free, with allocated-bytes before and after; the SPATIAL_START_IMPLICIT docstring matches the code and the explicit-start branch aborts when the reference view is index 0 or N-1; S7 has a real truthy parse, an explicit caller argument instead of an import-time env read, and no docstring claim that a dead guard protects anything.

phases.name: Phase 3 — Verify the comparison without touching the method
phases.goal: Answer the two questions a reviewer asks first — 'which SAM 2 is that, exactly' and 'is the comparison apples-to-apples' — plus close the one equivalence hole in the memory claim. All runs write to new folders; the frozen result is never overwritten. GPU-bound, so it interleaves with Phase 2's authoring work.
phases.rationale: The baseline claim 'SAM 2 tops out at 0.8434' selects the best of six columns whose configurations are recorded nowhere, and they are not near-duplicates — Dog is 0.7662 vs 0.9089 across two of them, FlameSteak 0.4627 vs 0.7835. Worse, the 2026-09-04 recheck (jf_recheck.json, CoffeeMartini) reproduces SegMaskNew3 exactly at 0.8060/0.8644/0.8352 and does NOT reproduce the cited headline column SegMaskNew1 at 0.8084/0.8675/0.8380 — so the one baseline column verified reproducible today is not the one the paper cites. Picking the strongest baseline is the conservative choice; being unable to say which system produced it is not. sam2-xview-pair is the cheapest high-value item here: if sam2_demoVideo_maskSingleInputMVSeg.py (SCSam2Video, no cross-view) and sam2_demoVideoNew_maskSingleInputMVSeg.py (SCSam2VideoNew, cross-view) differ only in the mechanism, then the SAM 2 lineage already contains its own on/off pair and the paired delta is computable with no GPU: +0.0014, 11/15 wins, CI [-0.0000, +0.0034] — the same mechanism at the same size in a second model family, which is a far stronger argument than one uncontrolled SAM 3 comparison. The guard is REPORT M8's note that SAM 2 batches all objects into one state per camera (SCSam2VideoNew.py:123-142) while SAM 3 uses per-object states, so if the pair also differs in session structure we say so rather than citing it. sam2-config-match and fill-hole-area are two halves of the same question: REPORT E6 shows three settings differ between the arms — SAM 2 runs fill_hole_area=8 applied at 256² (~250 px full-res) while SCSam3Video.py:17,20 monkey-patches SAM 3's to 0 against a builder default of 16, SAM 3 applies non-overlap to its output and SAM 2 does not, and low-res is 288 vs 256 — and the claimed SAM 3 advantage is almost entirely boundary F (+0.006), the same magnitude as those knobs. Testing 8 and 16 on the SAM 3 side costs one sweep and is the cheapest untested knob in the pipeline; the sign is genuinely unknown. heavy3-equivalence closes the one structural hole in the memory claim: byte-identity is proven on 12 datasets / 12,692 PNGs plus a from-scratch original re-run, but AlexaMeadeExhibit, CoffeeMartini and FlameSteak have no equivalence control at all because the original code cannot run — precisely the three entries that make '15/15 completes' worth saying. Restrict frames, never cameras (operations.md trap 1: `--track-cams written` is a different model for NewMem-family algorithms and raises IndexError at output_dicts[-4] with 3 sessions), run under --memory=90g, and the claim goes from unverifiable to verified-on-a-prefix. timing-matched turns a liability into a result: REPORT E5 shows the '2-3x slower' impression is 46 sessions vs 3, and per view-frame the New variant is faster (0.44 s vs 0.56 s) with the cross-view pass costing 16 s vs 15 s — cross-view memory is roughly free, which the paper currently cannot state. crossview-seed-oracle gives the benchmark its missing upper reference by seeding each scored camera from its own GT frame-0 mask; paired with Phase 1's seed census it splits the error budget into 'stage-1 seeding' and 'stage-2 tracking' and bounds Phase 5's seed-repair headroom before we build it.
phases.exit_criteria: Every SAM 2 folder in the results table names its generating script and config, and the cited baseline column is reproduced from a current run rather than inherited; a matched SAM 2 arm (apply_postprocessing=False, non_overlap_masks=True) exists and the F +0.006 is either confirmed as boundary quality or reassigned to post-processing, with the unmatchable 288-vs-256 knob stated; the SAM 2 cross-view on/off pair is either cited as an independent replication or explicitly ruled out with the session-structure reason; the three heavy datasets have a frames-restricted byte-identity check between baseline-onestagenew and MVOpt; a per-view-frame timing column with matched session counts exists; a GT-seeded per-camera ceiling row exists for all 15 datasets; fill_hole_area ∈ {0, 8, 16} is measured on SAM 3 and the chosen value appears in the runMVSeg banner.

phases.name: Phase 4 — The fork point: hygiene fixes and the in-package W=0 control
phases.goal: Land the two one-line correctness fixes that the entire accuracy programme is blocked on, make the cross-view window a parameter, and run the W=0 vs W=4 comparison that is the first valid control the method has ever had. This is the first phase that deliberately changes published output, which is why it comes after the harness, the manifest and the honest baseline.
phases.rationale: Both defects are confirmed live: SCSam3TrackerPredictorNewMem.py:1264 is still `for s_pos in range(-4, 0)` with `output_dicts[prev_spatial_idx]` indexed three lines later and no bounds check, so views 0..3 wrap to the last cameras; and :1273 still reads `selected_cond_outputs, unselected_cond_outputs1 = select_closest_cond_frames(...)`, rebinding the outer variable that is consumed as the cond object pointer at :1335-1341. Anyone grepping for the new `unselected_cond_outputs1` name will wrongly conclude C2 landed. The consequence is not cosmetic: where the neighbour object was zero-mask seeded the pointer is `no_obj_ptr` with object_score_logits = -10, an explicit 'object absent' signal injected into a view where the object is present, and REPORT E2 confirms this is why the eight index-0 cameras differ from OneStage on every frame after the seed. SCHEDULE:349 and :421 are emphatic that these are deliberate output changes that must land after the bit-identity baseline so the delta can be attributed, and :423 that they must ship together because the wrap is exactly what makes the C2 fallback execute every frame. The upper bound is small — index-0 camera means differ by at most ±0.0015 today and that difference is the C2 effect, so ≤8 of 36 cameras move by ≤0.0015, roughly ≲0.0004 on the headline — but per-(obj,frame) |ΔJ| reaches 0.49 (Fencing v0 f17) and 0.43 (Barn v0), and the injected signal is unambiguously wrong. The decision this phase forces, and it must be made before the runs rather than after: W=4-with-hygiene is a different system from the frozen 0.8451, so the paper picks one family and reports it end to end. Do not print a hygiene-fixed W curve next to the frozen headline. closure-track-mode is the enabler, not a nicety — REPORT P2 argues that because the window is one-sided and lockstep ascends, scored view v depends only on views 0..v, so `closure` (range(0, max(scored_idx)+1)) is output-identical to `all` once the C1 guard lands, and it cuts Welder from 553 s to ~60 s and AlexaMeade from 945 to 84 view-frames. With five W values across 15 datasets at 35-90 min per all-views sweep on one GPU, that difference is what makes the grid a week rather than a month. Verify it with `diff -rq` (experiment-plan row 6) rather than assuming it. xview-window-param is the instrument: `range(-self.cross_view_window, 0)`, a constructor argument threaded through build_scsam3.py:494-548, a SCSAM3_XVIEW_WINDOW env var, and `--xview-window N` routing output to SegMaskSam3XW{N}, with W ≤ 6 a hard cap because maskmem_tpos_enc has seven rows. I confirmed no `xview`, `cross_view_window` or `XVIEW` token exists anywhere in runMVSeg.py or build_scsam3.py, and `--track-cams` still offers only {written, all}. config-surfacing rides along because the window becomes an argument anyway; the same edit should surface fill_hole_area and track_cams in the banner at runMVSeg.py:271-279 and annotate the upstream params that are inert on the NewMem path (hotstart 15/8/8, recondition_every_nth_frame=16, keep_alive 30 at build_scsam3.py:927-937), which a reader of that file reasonably concludes are active. Read the results on Phase 1's endpoints — nonref, nb bins, paired test — not on the headline: REPORT E1's own arithmetic says anything under ~+0.005 is indistinguishable from noise on 15 datasets.
phases.exit_criteria: The negative-index guard and the `_,` rebinding fix are in demoSCSam3MVOpt and each is covered by a Phase 2 test that fails if reverted; `--track-cams closure` exists and `diff -rq` shows zero differences against `--track-cams all` on Blocks, Fencing and Welder; `--xview-window N` routes to SegMaskSam3XW{N} and W=0 empties the neighbour loop; SegMaskSam3XW0 and SegMaskSam3XW4 exist for all 15 datasets with manifests, and the net effect of cross-view memory is reported as row4 − row3 on the non-reference split with nb bins and a paired per-camera test rather than on the headline alone; a written decision records which family (frozen or hygiene-fixed) is the paper's headline; the runMVSeg banner prints window, fill_hole_area and track_cams.

phases.name: Phase 5 — Targeted accuracy, now decidable rather than speculative
phases.goal: Attack the two measured losses against SAM 2 — Welder −0.034 and Fencing −0.021 — plus the protocol artefact that suppresses every method, each against the Phase 4 control so the result can be attributed. Ordered by how much evidence the docs actually carry.
phases.rationale: seed-repair goes first because it is the only item with a measured target rather than an inference. REPORT A3 establishes that Welder's entire −0.034 is camera_0004: the spatial pass seeds objects 8 and 14 with 4 px and 7 px against GT of 13,268 and 18,899 px, and object 12 at IoU 0.184, while the SAM 2 spatial pass seeds the same three at IoU 0.94/0.93/0.90 and tracks them at J 0.93/0.93/0.90. The bad seed is then pinned in cond memory and the cond pointer, and cross-view memory demonstrably cannot overturn it — measured ΔJ +0.0004 even though views 0/1/2 hold the object — so this is a class of failure the temporal mechanism is structurally unable to fix. P5 quantifies the repair at Welder +0.035~0.04, roughly +0.0023..0.0027 on the 15-dataset average, which is larger than the entire current margin over SAM 2. It is gated on Phase 1's degenerate-seed census bounding the upside and on confirming by log that the refine branch at SCSam3VideoInference.py:1855-1870 adds a cond frame to the same tracker state rather than creating a new one (use_stateless_refinement=False) — reviewers split 2-1 on that, so it is a logged check, not an assumption. Hard constraint: re-propagate with an implicit start, never an explicit start_frame_index (investigations-closed #4, Blocks 0.7484 → 0.2827). Mirror it in runMVSegForSam2.py so the baseline stays comparable. two-sided-window is second because its number is explicitly an inference: REPORT P4 labels the Fencing v0 J 0.80 → ~0.86 projection as inferred, not measured. The structural argument is nonetheless the strongest in the audit — of 36 scored cameras 8 are index 0 and 6 of those are the reference camera, so the recovery mechanism is absent from a third of the benchmark by construction, and the same two Fencing objects that sit at J 0.32/0.23 at v0 recover to 0.55/0.58 at v9 where four neighbours exist. Under lockstep a true same-frame two-sided window is impossible, so only the t−1 fallback form is implementable; ring wrap stays off for the LLFF scenes (Blocks/Fencing/Carpark are open arcs); and `seq_len` must be recomputed from the neighbour feats rather than reused from :1283 (C8). reference-rule-count is the protocol half of ceiling-refrule: runMVSeg.py:111 is still `n = int(np.max(img))` while the docstring at :98-103 claims 'most objects', and objects absent from the reference seed frame get a zero prompt, are dropped by the zero-area filter at SCSam3VideoInference.py:464, never register, and score J=F=0 forever — 1,579 of 21,651 scored pairs. Switching to `len(np.unique(img))-1` behind `--reference {count,maxid,<cam>}` drops structural zeros Blocks 203→63, MATF 372→231, PoznanStreet 42→0. It is rank-invariant by construction (it lifts every method equally, so all three must be re-run under it) and raises the headline without being evidence for the method — say so in the table. neighbor-objptr is the one token-conditioning variant all three reviewers converged on: the neighbour obj_ptr is 256-d, already GPU-resident, and completely unread, while in SAM 3 the pointer is what carries the object/no-object decision, so the most natural cross-view existence channel is empty. Success bar is >+0.005 on nonref with no reference-camera loss. view-order and ref-view-sensitivity are the two variance questions a multi-view reviewer will ask: the neighbour set is 'the W predecessors in session-list order' and that order comes from a demo literal (sam3_demoVideo.py:17 = [0..7,16..31,8..15], and Dog's perms skip cameras outright), so the result currently encodes list order rather than camera geometry — a negative result there is publishable as a stated limitation. And with runs bit-identical run-to-run (REPORT.md:40-44, 41/45 cameras identical across two sweeps) there is no seed variance to report, so reference choice is the only error bar available, and there is exactly one draw per dataset behind a margin of 0.0017.
phases.exit_criteria: Welder camera_0004 objects 8/14/12 move from J 0/0/0.14 to ≥0.8 with control datasets (Carpark, Frog) within ±0.001, or seed-repair is abandoned with the diagnostic recorded; the two-sided window is measured against the Phase 4 W=4 arm on the six datasets where the effect exists, with the nb=0 bin delta reported as the decisive readout; the count reference rule is run for all three methods on the five affected datasets and the ranking is shown unchanged; the neighbour-pointer variant is judged against its stated >+0.005-on-nonref bar; a view-order sensitivity result and a reference-view spread exist and are reported as the paper's error bar. Every result in this phase is read on the non-reference split with a paired test, never on the headline alone.

phases.name: Phase 6 — Deferred engineering, opportunistic
phases.goal: Clear the debt that neither blocks a result nor risks one, in whatever slack the sweeps leave. Nothing here is on the critical path.
phases.rationale: seeding-response-skip is pure speed with an output-identity claim both reviewers already cleared (SCHEDULE:327) — it was held only because it arrived bundled with the trim patch, and SCHEDULE:329 requires it be resubmitted fully separated and re-cleared. Seeding drops from 120 s (AlexaMeade) / 217 s (CoffeeMartini) / 260 s (FlameSteak) to seconds. The one hard constraint is that it must never be enabled on the cross-view session (AddReferenceMask, runMVSeg.py:184-190), because :190 reads out_obj_ids, which is a product of the filtering being skipped. Its persistent GPU saving is redundant with S1, so the unique win is time — worth having before the Phase 5 grids, not worth delaying them for. twostage-verify-or-revert is a decision, not a task: demoSCSam3TwoStage and TwoStageNew carry hand-edited memory patches (3 and 4 files, ~200 lines) that no execution has ever touched, neither appears in runMVSeg.py:38-40's ALGOS nor in runMVSegForSam2.py (ALGO_DIR is hard-coded to demoSCSam3ForSam2New at :26), and they passed syntax check only. open-items.md:41-46 recommends reverting if they will not be registered. The urgency changed since that was written — the edits are committed in 3232d3e and permanently in history — but Phase 0's baseline-siblings tag makes the revert one command. If they are registered instead, NEEDS_ALL_VIEWS membership must be settled first (TwoStageNew shares cross-view memory via spatial_idx=m per patch-matrix.md:96, so it likely needs `all`), or trap 1 applies. forsam2new-s6-retire is the highest-value engineering item and the only one with a quantified target: demoSCSam3ForSam2New/SCSam3Video.py:14-15 builds two complete models that both stay resident, `grep -c RetireSpatialPredictor` over all 14 .py files in that folder and over runMVSegForSam2.py returns 0 everywhere, and patch-matrix.md:68 explicitly marks S6 as applicable-but-not-applied there. operations.md:138-140 credits retire as the direct cause of Welder fitting inside the 90 GiB cap for MVOpt, worth ~3.2 GiB of weights plus ~1.6 GiB of pinned autocast copies, and investigations-closed #10 records CoffeeMartini and FlameSteak dying at 45.81 GiB on a 48 GiB card at exactly the moment retire would fire — on entry to temporal tracking, after the cross-view pass completes. This does not re-open #10, which closed the different hypothesis that S1-S5 could be copied across. The folder-specific hazard is that predictor_spatial.backbone is an alias of model_spatial.detector.backbone (SCSam3Video.py:21), so both handles must be dropped or nothing frees, and masks_spatial must be confirmed to be fresh tensors rather than views into state. forsam2new-path-analysis is the queued second hypothesis if S6 falls short — open-items.md:36 and investigations-closed #10 both name it as the outstanding action and both forbid the copy-the-patches shortcut that was already disproved.
phases.exit_criteria: return_output=False is in a patch containing nothing else, re-reviewed, proven output-identical by `diff -rq` on at least two datasets, and provably never reachable from the cross-view session; TwoStage/TwoStageNew are either registered in ALGOS with a settled NEEDS_ALL_VIEWS membership and one successful cheap-dataset run each, or reverted to baseline-siblings — no third state; ForSam2New either completes the three heavy datasets after S6 or has a written path analysis naming where the remaining ~4-5 GiB of residency lives.

dropped: h1-trim-cached-outputs — Already done. Shipped 2026-09-04 as memory optimization S7 (SCSAM3_TRIM_CACHED_OUTPUTS); I verified SCSam3VideoInferenceNewMem.py:38 and :540-558 implement the strictly-past window SCHEDULE:315-318 required. Its residual defects (dead propagation_full guard, loose env parse) are scheduled as s7-flag-and-dead-guard in Phase 2. Note the numbering trap: SCHEDULE's held S5/H1 is memory-optimization.md's S7.

h3-fp16-frames — Explicitly forbidden and superseded. SCHEDULE:271-273 and :331-333 record that REPORT.md:183's 'results identical' claim for fp16 was disproved in verification: the 10-bit mantissa is unrecoverable by the consumer's fp32 cast at sam3/model/sam3_image.py:152 and the ~1e-3 error flips pixels at the `> 0.0` threshold in runMVSeg.py:328.
